authored_by: this lane, by hand, at the owner's instruction
WHAT_THIS_IS: A MOCKUP. Every Hebrew string below was typed by hand. None of it came from the corpus, none of it traces to a record, and none of it is a reading. It exists to show what each part of the frame LOOKS LIKE when it works, because the books that carry these marks are not published and one of them is not held at all.
WHY_IT_BREAKS_THE_RULE: The serve law says the pipeline decides and gates are the only judges, and this project does not ship proofs of concept. The owner set that rule and the owner suspended it here, for this block only, and said so plainly. What is not suspended is the requirement that a reader can tell the difference: every demonstration below is fenced, labelled, and refused a licence chip, because a licence chip on a typed string would be the one lie this site cannot afford.
WHAT_WOULD_MAKE_EACH_ONE_REAL: Named per demonstration in blocks_the_real_thing. Three are blocked by markup bleeding into the text of books we hold; one is blocked because nobody holds it.

demonstrations.title: written one way, read another
demonstrations.the_source_wrote: both forms at one site: round brackets around the written, square around the read
demonstrations.the_card_says: One word block, one card, two branches. Selecting a half underlines that half in the line and shows that half's English only — one English at a time, and neither is chosen for the reader.
demonstrations.key: keyed — one key per branch, delimiters stripped
demonstrations.blocks_the_real_thing: This site holds Daniel and cannot build it: 332 of its surfaces carry literal HTML markup where the text should be.

demonstrations.title: an open section
demonstrations.the_card_says: The word — petuchah, open — and what it does: this section ends here, and the next begins on a fresh line. If the reader cannot give the break its line, the card says so in plain English rather than drawing nothing.
demonstrations.key: unkeyed — the letter here abbreviates a word and is not an occurrence of that letter
demonstrations.blocks_the_real_thing: Amos is held for the same markup defect. Eight books that do arrive clean arrived flattened, with the marks already gone.

demonstrations.title: a closed section
demonstrations.the_card_says: The word — setumah, closed — and what it does: this section ends, and the next begins on the same line, after a gap. A reader that draws this the same as an open section has erased a distinction the scribe made, and has to say which one it cannot honor.
demonstrations.blocks_the_real_thing: Exodus is held: 74 surfaces carry literal markup.

demonstrations.title: a passage set apart
demonstrations.the_card_says: The mark's name, and what the tradition says with it: this passage stands apart. Whether it opens, closes, or stands alone is recorded — in Psalm 107 these stand singly, here two of them bracket the passage — and no partner is demanded.
demonstrations.key: unkeyed — this is a punctuation character, not the letter nun
demonstrations.blocks_the_real_thing: Seven of these are in the body. Numbers is one of the eight books that arrived flattened.

demonstrations.title: one word, or the words it stands for

options.reading: the abbreviation as written, defined as itself

cells.english: the Holy One, blessed be He

options.reading: the words it stands for, each defined separately

demonstrations.the_card_says: An abbreviation is an ordinary COMPspan with two options, not a special case. Selecting the second does not change one letter of what is printed — the page still shows what the source wrote. The lattice chooses what gets DEFINED, never what gets DISPLAYED, exactly as with written/read.
demonstrations.what_needs_attesting: not the words — each is attested elsewhere in the corpus and the cell points at it — but the MAPPING, that these letters stand for those words.
demonstrations.blocks_the_real_thing: Nothing. This one works on the published site today; it is shown here beside the others so the set can be read together.

demonstrations.title: the book's own count of itself
demonstrations.the_source_wrote: the scribes' bookkeeping, which states the total and the midpoint
demonstrations.why_three_midpoints: because they land in different places.
demonstrations.the_card_says: That this is not a word of the book, and what the scribes recorded here — then the ordinary card beneath it. The banner stands above a normal card, never instead of one.
demonstrations.counts: OFF — these are excluded from every count the book reports, or the total disagrees with the masorah's own figure and the fault is charged to the scribe
demonstrations.key: keyed, and the only OFF kind that is — these are ordinary Hebrew words meaning what they say
demonstrations.why_no_numbers_are_shown: Because the only honest states are NOT_HELD, HELD_UNCOUNTED, VERIFIED and CONTRADICTED, and HELD_UNCOUNTED may not be cited anywhere a reader can see. Printing a figure here would be citing an assumption. This is the only mark that makes a checkable claim, so recording it is not attesting it — the half has to be counted.
demonstrations.blocks_the_real_thing: Nobody holds it. The end-of-book masorah is missing from every Tanakh stream either lane has.

the_fence: The list above is exhaustive and is what the gate checks. Every Hebrew character the front door prints is either carried from a record or is one of these strings; a glyph that is neither fails check-poc-fenced-v1. That is what keeps a suspended rule from becoming an absent one.
